network_author.description: Build a rectangular grid network with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

x_length.description: Length in metres of an x-direction edge. SUMO: 100.

x_number.description: Junctions along x, at least 2. SUMO: 5.

y_length.description: Length in metres of a y-direction edge. SUMO: 100.

y_number.description: Junctions along y, at least 2. SUMO: 5.

network_author.name: generate_grid

network_author.description: Build a spider-web network (arms crossed by concentric circles) with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

arm_number.description: Number of arms, at least 3. SUMO: 13.

circle_number.description: Number of circles, at least 1. SUMO: 20.

omit_center.description: Leave out the central junction. SUMO: false.

space_radius.description: Distance in metres between circles. SUMO: 100.

network_author.name: generate_spider

network_author.description: Build a random network with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. The seed is required: the same seed and parameters give the same network. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

iterations.description: Number of random growth steps, at least 1. SUMO: 200.

max_distance.description: Maximum distance in metres, at least min_distance. SUMO: 250.

min_distance.description: Minimum distance in metres between nodes. SUMO: 100.

seed.description: Seed of the generator, at least 0.

network_author.name: generate_random

network_edit.description: Remove an edge, and every connection that starts or ends on it, from a network and recompile. Returns the new net_artifact and the modification to put in the recipe, or `unresolved` when the edge does not exist.

net_path.description: `net_artifact.path` of the .net.xml to edit, from an earlier tool.

network_edit.name: remove_edge

network_edit.description: Add an edge between two junctions that already exist and recompile; SUMO guesses its connections. A junction that does not exist is not created: the result is `unresolved` with needed_tool `add_node`. Returns the new net_artifact and the modification to put in the recipe.

edge_id.description: Id the new edge gets; by default the two junction ids joined.

from_junction.description: Id of the junction it leaves.

net_path.description: `net_artifact.path` of the .net.xml to edit, from an earlier tool.

to_junction.description: Id of the junction it enters.

network_edit.name: add_edge

network_edit.description: Set the number of lanes of an existing edge and recompile. Connections on a lane that no longer exists move to the outermost remaining lane. Returns the new net_artifact and the modification to put in the recipe, or `unresolved` when the edge does not exist.

lanes.description: New number of lanes, at least 1.

net_path.description: `net_artifact.path` of the .net.xml to edit, from an earlier tool.

network_edit.name: set_lanes

network_edit.description: Set the speed limit of an existing edge, all its lanes included, and recompile. Returns the new net_artifact and the modification to put in the recipe, or `unresolved` when the edge does not exist.

net_path.description: `net_artifact.path` of the .net.xml to edit, from an earlier tool.

speed.description: New speed limit in m/s, above 0.

network_edit.name: set_speed

network_find.description: List the stored networks whose label is exactly the name, case ignored. Returns `candidates`, each with its `network_id`, `label` and the network it `derived_from`. One candidate that is what the user means: answer Found with its id. None: build the network, or ask the user when it cannot be built. Several: ask the user which one.

name.description: The network reference, as the user wrote it.

network_find.name: find_network

network_import.description: Find where a place or point of interest is (a hospital, a square, a station, an address), so the area you download is drawn from data and not from memory. Returns its `lat`, `lon` and what it is (`category`, `type`, `name`), or `not_found` when the geocoder does not know it: then try another wording (the official name, with the city, in Catalan or Spanish). `verify_coverage` reports how far the network ends from every place located in this run.

query.description: The place, with the city, e.g. 'Hospital Moisès Broggi, Sant Joan Despí' or 'Plaça de Francesc Macià, Barcelona'.

network_import.name: locate_place

network_import.description: List the import profiles `netconvert` can use (what the imported network keeps: roads, rail, bicycle lanes, pedestrian paths) and the vehicle classes `keep_vclass` accepts. Public transport stops and lines and polygons are not part of any profile.
network_import.name: list_import_profiles

network_import.description: Download the OpenStreetMap data of an area of interest, once per polygon (a second call for the same area reuses the stored snapshot). Name the area with exactly one of `bbox`, `polygon` or `place_name` (an administrative boundary, resolved to a polygon). Put any extra thing the user asked for in `requirements`, for example 'bus stops'. Returns the `source` and the `osm_snapshot` for the recipe, or `needs_user` when the area is above the size limit, the place is not a boundary, or a requirement is unsupported (public transport stops and lines); then nothing was downloaded.

place_name.description: Name of an administrative area, e.g. 'Sant Antoni'.

polygon.description: Closed ring of [lat, lon] points, at most about 200 vertices.

requirements.description: What else the user asked for, in their words, e.g. ['bus stops'].

network_import.name: fetch_osm

network_import.description: The streets of a fetched snapshot, longest first: name, ref (e.g. 'N-340'), road classes, total length and extent. Highways with no name and no ref are grouped by class. Use it before `select_streets` to see how the streets the user named are spelled, and whether the road changes name along the stretch. With `near`, only the streets that pass within `radius_m` of that point. At most 40 rows.

near.description: [lat, lon] of a point, e.g. one `locate_place` returned.

network_import.name: list_streets

network_import.description: Find the road a car takes between two points of a fetched snapshot (the quickest, from the speed limits), and which streets to select to keep it. A road often changes name on the way, or has only a ref (a motorway): the trace follows it anyway. Returns its stretches (`route`), `total_m`, `minutes`, where each point was put on a road (`snapped`), the first and last point on the suggested streets (`joins_at`, `leaves_at`) and `suggested_selection`, to pass as it is to `select_streets`. Returns `not_reached` with the box to `fetch_osm` instead when a point is outside the fetched area or less than 300 m from its edge, or when no road joins the two points (a point more than 500 m from any road that does).

prefer.description: Streets the user named, as names or parts of names (any case) or refs, e.g. ['Avinguda Diagonal', 'B-23']: when two roads take about as long, the trace keeps to these, and the suggested selection includes the ones it touches.

network_import.name: trace_corridor

network_import.description: Keep only some streets of a fetched snapshot, before `netconvert`: every highway whose name contains one of `names`, or whose ref is one of `refs` (a road that changes name keeps its ref), plus every road in the `areas` you give (cut to the stretch inside the zone), plus the `connectors` you ask for, minus what the `drop` rules remove (a removed road never comes back as a connector). Use names and refs for a stretch you know; use an area for a place you want in full detail (a motorway junction, a roundabout, a municipality's accesses), then drop the classes or streets you do not want. Writes a new snapshot and returns its `osm_snapshot` and `source` for the recipe; build it with `netconvert` like any other. Also returns what was kept, what each area added, what each rule removed (0 when nothing) and in how many `pieces`: more than one means gaps a vehicle cannot cross. Fails when nothing matches; then check the names with `list_streets`. Trying another selection downloads nothing.

areas.description: Zones to keep whole: every road with a node inside, cut to the stretch inside. The same `near` and `radius_m` as `list_streets`.

items.description: A zone: every road with a node within `radius_m` of `near`.

near.description: [lat, lon] of the centre of the zone.

radius_m.description: Radius of the zone in metres. Default 300.

connectors.description: Which other ways join the pieces of the selection: 'none'; 'links', only `*_link` ramps; 'all', any road (links, squares and crossings with another name), at most 300 m long. Default 'all'.

drop.description: Rules that remove roads from the selection. With `near` (and `radius_m`) a rule removes only inside that zone. A rule with no name, ref or class is an error.

items.description: A rule: removes the roads that match any of its criteria, inside its zone when it has one.

near.description: [lat, lon] of the centre of the zone.

radius_m.description: Radius of the zone in metres. Default 300.

names.description: Names or parts of names, any case, e.g. ['Avinguda Diagonal'].

network_import.name: select_streets

network_import.description: Build the network from a fetched snapshot with `netconvert`: the chosen import profile, cut to the area's polygon, keeping the largest connected component. Starts the cleanups again. Returns the `netconvert_options` and `net_artifact` for the recipe, or `needs_user` when the network has more edges than one import allows.
network_import.name: netconvert

network_import.description: Rebuild keeping only the largest connected component, so no piece of road is cut off from the rest. `netconvert` already does it; this makes the choice explicit after other cleanups. Returns the updated options.
network_import.name: keep_largest_component

network_import.description: Rebuild removing isolated edges (edges that connect to nothing at either end).
network_import.name: remove_isolated

network_import.description: Rebuild joining junctions that are close together (a big crossing mapped as several nodes) into one.
network_import.name: join_junctions

network_import.description: Rebuild keeping only the edges that allow a vehicle class, for example 'passenger' to drop rail and pedestrian-only paths.
network_import.name: keep_vclass

network_import.description: Is the network you last built from a snapshot the one the user asked for? Returns its extent; its connected components with their ends; the streets of the snapshot with stretches that did not make it into the network (where they are and how long); and, for every place `locate_place` found in this run, how far the network and its nearest end are from it. Call it before you submit a network of selected streets; what it shows and you cannot fix goes to unresolved[] with its numbers.
network_import.name: verify_coverage

network_inspection.description: A bounded summary of a network: edge, junction and traffic light counts, total length, speed range, road types, vehicle classes, connected components and a short list of suspect edges (zero length, isolated, with no outgoing connection).

net_path.description: Path of the .net.xml to look at, as a tool that built it returned it.

network_inspection.name: inspect_network

network_inspection.description: One edge of a network: endpoints, length, speed, lanes, road type, allowed vehicle classes and the edges it leads to.

net_path.description: Path of the .net.xml to look at, as a tool that built it returned it.

network_inspection.name: inspect_edge

network_inspection.description: Is the network sound? Returns the share of edges in the largest strongly connected component, the number of zero-length edges, whether every edge can be reached from the border, and whether the three together pass.

net_path.description: Path of the .net.xml to look at, as a tool that built it returned it.

network_inspection.name: sanity_check

network_inspection.description: Simulate light random demand on a network with SUMO to see whether it jams. Returns teleports, collisions, vehicles that did not arrive, the edges where vehicles waited most and the SUMO statistics file as evidence. Nothing is stored as a result.

net_path.description: Path of the .net.xml to look at, as a tool that built it returned it.

seed.description: Seed of the demand and of SUMO. Default 0.

vehicles.description: Number of random trips, 1 to 2000. Default 100.

network_inspection.name: probe_run
